# go-modern-reflect-type-for

**Since:** Go 1.22

## Summary

Use `reflect.TypeFor[T]()` instead of `reflect.TypeOf((*T)(nil)).Elem()`.

## Details

reflect.TypeFor returns the reflect.Type for a compile-time type parameter or type argument.
It avoids nil-pointer tricks and is clearer for interface types.

## Examples

### Before

```go
typ := reflect.TypeOf((*T)(nil)).Elem()
```

### After

```go
typ := reflect.TypeFor[T]()
```

Source: [https://github.com/JetBrains/go-modern-guidelines/blob/main/internal/guidelines/guidelines.json](https://github.com/JetBrains/go-modern-guidelines/blob/main/internal/guidelines/guidelines.json)
